title: Non-Hermitian Purcell Physics in Dissipatively Coupled Planar Photon-Magnon Systems
authors: Shubham Singh, Sachin Verma, Animesh Chakraworty, Abhishek Maurya, Biswanath Bhoi, Rajeev Singh
abstract: The Purcell effect has emerged as a powerful mechanism for controlling spontaneous emission and dissipation in cavity and nanophotonic systems; however, its realization in dissipative non-Hermitian hybrid platforms remains largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate the Purcell effect in a dissipatively coupled photon-magnon hybrid quantum system consisting of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) thin film integrated with an inverted octa-ring resonator (IORR) in a planar geometry. To describe the underlying dissipative hybrid dynamics, we develop a quantum theoretical framework based on non-Hermitian coupled-mode theory combined with the input-output formalism. We also analyze the temporal decay dynamics of the photon-magnon system. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate that the system can be engineered to operate in the level-attraction regime through dissipative photon-magnon coupling. By systematically tuning the magnon damping, we uncover the emergence of a Purcell regime in which cavity-photon dissipation is selectively enhanced through magnon-mediated loss channels. We further show that the saturation magnetization (Ms) provides an additional degree of control over the onset, tunability, and robustness of the Purcell enhancement. The combined modulation of magnon damping and Ms strongly influences the effective photon-magnon coupling, hybrid-mode evolution, and dissipation landscape, enabling precise control of hybrid quantum states. These findings establish a versatile strategy for engineering magnetization- and dissipation-controlled photon-magnon interactions in planar, chip-compatible architectures, opening new avenues for non-Hermitian cavity magnonics, tunable microwave dissipation engineering, and hybrid quantum information technologies.
summary: This paper explores controlling the Purcell effect in a planar photon-magnon system by treating the coupling and dissipation using non-Hermitian quantum theory. By systematically tuning magnon damping and magnetization, the authors show they can engineer the system into a regime where cavity photon decay is selectively enhanced by magnon-mediated losses. This establishes a versatile, chip-compatible method for controlling hybrid quantum dissipation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the realization and control of the Purcell effect in hybrid quantum systems where photon and magnon dynamics are coupled and subject to dissipation.
main_result: The study demonstrates that engineered magnon damping and saturation magnetization can be used to drive the system into a Purcell regime, enabling precise control over cavity-photon dissipation.
method: The authors developed a quantum theoretical framework using non-Hermitian coupled-mode theory and the input-output formalism, validated by full-wave electromagnetic simulations.
model_or_system: The system models a planar hybrid quantum platform consisting of an Inverted Octagon-Ring Resonator (IORR) photon cavity coupled to a Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG) magnon film. The dynamics are described by an open-system Hamiltonian incorporating coherent and dissipative photon-magnon coupling.
key_observables: Purcell factor ($F_P$), effective cavity decay rate ($ eta$), hybrid-mode spectra, and time-domain decay profiles.
important_parameters: Magnon damping parameter ($\alpha$), Saturation Magnetization ($M_s$), and the ratio of coherent to dissipative coupling ($J$ vs. $\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the system can be modeled effectively using non-Hermitian quantum mechanics and that the explored parameter space is experimentally accessible.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup, the quantum coupled-mode model, and simulation results showing the dependence of decay rates and Purcell factors on damping and coupling strength.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework (non-Hermitian theory) to simulating the system response by varying key parameters ($\alpha$ and $M_s$), culminating in the demonstration of controlled Purcell enhancement via dissipation engineering.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems as it provides a concrete, tunable platform (magnonics) to study non-Hermitian physics, level attraction, and engineered dissipation effects, which are central topics in modern quantum optics.

The substrate thickness is 0.6 mm, and the ground plane thickness is 35 µm. The inverted octagonal-ring resonator (IORR) has an outer radius of a=3mm, an inner radius of b=2mm, and a gap of g =0.64mm. The YIG film dimensions are 4mm x 4mm x 20 µm , while the microstrip line has a width of 0.57 mm and a thickness of 35 µm. (b) Schematic diagram of the quantum coupled-mode model.

Spintronics.note: The paper directly models the coupling between cavity photons and magnons (spin waves) in a planar hybrid system, which is a core topic of cavity QED in magnets and magnon/photon polaritons.
